status.main_product: Supply chain finance and invoice discounting platform
status.scope_reason: The company operates a domestic TReDS platform (DTX) and an IFSCA-licensed cross-border trade finance platform (GTX) providing receivables discounting and supply chain financing.
status.evidence: According to The Economic Times, KredX secured a license from the Reserve Bank of India in January 2025 to operate its Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) platform.

claims.claim: The company reports offering import financing, external commercial borrowing, and buyer's credit capabilities via its global marketplace network.
The company reports that its platform integrates with the MonetaGo Secure Financing system to perform real-time validation against duplicate invoice financing risks.

KredX announced a strategic partnership in August 2025 under which its Domestic Trade Exchange (DTX) platform utilizes MonetaGo's Secure Financing system, an application integrated into Swift's API-enabled infrastructure to prevent duplicate trade financing fraud.

In corporate insights published on its digital transformation portal, KredX highlights the theoretical operational benefits of moving toward electronic bills of lading (eBLs) and digital platform integrations, though it outlines these concepts conceptually rather than as active native features.
The company reports that its platforms are built on a scalable, secure microservice architecture combined with API integrations to deliver enterprise-grade fintech resilience.
claims.note: scalable secure microservice architecture combined with API integrations to deliver enterprise-grade fintech resilience

claims.claim: The company reports a transaction processing volume exceeding $12 billion across its ecosystem, serving more than 700 corporate clients and 15 financial institution partners.
The company reports building its Content Management System (CMS) with AI-powered cash posting and collection modules that automate 99% of cash posting and digitize any invoice format.
claims.corrected: The company reports building its Content Management System (CMS) with AI-powered cash posting and collection modules that automate 100% of touchless cash posting even in the case of exceptional scenarios, missing data & unfamiliar payment formats and digitize any invoice format.

claims.claim: The company reports integrating agentic AI into its TReDS financing platform to shorten corporate and vendor onboarding timelines and systematically manage credit risk.
The company reports onboarding over 3,000 enterprises and 100,000 MSMEs onto its supply chain finance platforms, including its Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) platform DTX.

The company has formed strategic financing partnerships with prominent Indian banking institutions, including alliances with ICICI Bank for a co-branded commercial card, and partnerships with Canara Bank and State Bank of India (SBI) to act as financiers on its DTX platform.
KredX reported an overall revenue of ₹41.61 crore for FY24 (representing 25% growth compared to ₹33.25 crore in FY23), which subsequently declined by 66.1% to ₹14.1 crore for FY25.
The company raised $26 million in a Series B funding round led by Tiger Global Management in December 2019, with participation from existing investors.
Prior to its Series B, the company raised a $6.25 million Series A funding round led by Sequoia Capital India (now Peak XV Partners) alongside Prime Venture Partners in October 2016.
The company reports a transaction volume of over USD 10 billion (and elsewhere over 12 billion), serving more than 700 corporates and over 40,000 to 150,000 businesses across its ecosystems.

The company reports partnerships with 15 financial institutions and over 30 financiers, including integrations and partnerships with institutions such as the State Bank of India (SBI) and Central Bank of India for its Domestic Trade Exchange (DTX) TReDS platform.
claims.source: KredX Official Website, RBI TReDS Statistics
